brief: A herb planter of three cells side by side, each with a bin that drains.

requirements.requirement: Three cells side by side (a straight row of three bases)
requirements.evidence: Three Hex base · Full pieces at axial cells (-1,0), (0,0), (1,0) on level 0, joined by joint bolts on both seams; check_build shows no LOOSE_BODY and meshClash clear.

requirements.requirement: Each of the three cells holds a bin
requirements.evidence: One hex-bin-full-drain bin in each of the three cells (bin:-1,0,0, bin:0,0,0, bin:1,0,0).

All three bins are the 'Bin, full depth, drained' variant (hex-bin-full-drain). The configurator confirms the variant, not that water actually drains; no cover was added, so the drainage is the bin's own. Material and drainage performance are unverified.
Each bin filled with soil and planted: basil-young in (-1,0), mint-young in (0,0), parsley-young in (1,0); no prop warnings.

finish.summary: Built a three-cell herb planter: three full hex bases in a straight row, each with a drained full-depth bin, joint-bolted, soil-filled and planted with basil, mint and parsley. check_build has no errors and meshClash is clear. Assembly note from the parts list: tighten the M6 bolts by hand to about 2 N.m, never with a cordless driver. Drainage is the bin's drain variant; I did not verify water flow.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
